goal: Make RPC and PSBT processing report internal I/O errors clearly instead of misreporting them as a missing transaction
Helps node operators and RPC consumers detect disk corruption or storage failures instead of getting a misleading result
reviewability: Stale: needs rebase and author has been silent for 62 days
Conflicts with several other open PRs touching the same files
agreement: Concept approval without stated objection to the overall approach (yuvicc, musaHaruna)
Unaddressed objection: pruned-block lookup may return a wrong error message, regression risk, no author reply (yuvicc)
Nonblocking objection: test should wrap file rename in try/finally, discussion stalled (musaHaruna)

categories.name: rpc
why: P3 because it fixes a real but rare correctness issue where I/O failures looked like missing transactions
Benefit is mainly for operators encountering disk corruption during RPC or PSBT calls
A possible pruned-node error-message regression remains unresolved, limiting confidence

categories.name: indexes
why: P3 because it improves correctness of the txindex error path so I/O failures surface rather than being masked
Matters mainly in low-frequency disk corruption or storage failure scenarios
Data integrity relevance is the main value here, not everyday user-facing benefit
